claim: SOLVENT's published receipt chain verifies end to end - every receipt's published hash is the canonical digest of its own body under the registered recipe, and every prev_hash is the preceding receipt's published hash - and it is a weaker trading record than 384 receipts suggest: fewer than half of its pre-trade commitments reach an execution the chain reports as confirmed on chain, fewer than a tenth of its execution seals carry a pre-trade anchor transaction, and no receipt carries a funding field, so the equity series the chain does carry cannot be read as a return.
falsifier: Four results refute the claim, one per limb, and any of them refutes it on its own. (1) If any of the 384 published hashes is not the canonical digest of its own receipt body under the registered recipe, or any prev_hash is not the preceding envelope's published hash, or the genesis prev_hash is not the zero word, the integrity limb is refuted and the report lists every failing seq rather than reporting a share. (2) If confirmed executions reach or exceed half of the pre-trade commitments - |confirmed| / |P| >= 0.5 - the reliability limb is refuted and the report says the chain reaches a confirmed execution for at least half of the intentions it states. (3) If seals carrying a pre_trade_anchor_tx_hash reach or exceed a tenth of all seals - |anchored| / |S| >= 0.1 - the coverage limb is refuted and the record may then be described as pre-committed on chain to that extent. (4) If the enumerated key paths of the 384 receipts contain any field recording money moving into or out of the account whose equity the receipts report, the funding limb is refuted, and a deposit-adjusted return is computed and published from it instead of this record's refusal to publish one. Two paths under an execution seal's verification block name the two legs of the single swap that seal reports, in the two tokens that swap moved; a leg of a trade is not a movement into or out of the account, by the definition registered here and not by anything observed in this corpus, so those two do not refute the limb. The whole key-path set is published so a reader applying a different definition can apply it to the same list. Whichever way each limb comes out is published: a chain that verifies is not a good trading record, and this claim says so in its own words, so surviving its falsifier is not a result in the agent's favour and is not to be read as one.

metric.formula:
Everything is read from the registered corpus and nothing is fetched while it is computed. The corpus is the server's own list of 384 {hash, receipt} envelopes.

CHAIN INTEGRITY, two limbs, both over all 384 envelopes. Content: for every envelope, the published hash must equal hash(receipt) = "0x" + sha256(json.dumps(receipt, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() over that envelope's own receipt object. Linkage: receipt[0].prev_hash must be the 32-byte zero word, and for every i>0 receipt[i].prev_hash must equal envelope[i-1]'s published hash. Each limb is reported as {numerator, denominator, value} over 384 and 384 respectively, and every failing seq is listed by number rather than counted. The recipe differs from docket.hire.receipts.canonical_hash in ensure_ascii alone, so the two agree on every receipt whose body is pure ASCII and can only disagree on the ones that are not; the count of receipts carrying a non-ASCII character, and the count on which the two recipes disagree, are both reported so a reader can see where the recipe was actually decided. The chain's head - envelope[383]'s published hash - and envelope[381]'s are both reported, because Docket's own v1 task 02 recorded on 2026-08-08 the head SOLVENT served and the value carried by the BSC anchor transaction at seq 381, and those two are an external check this corpus cannot forge for itself.

DENOMINATORS, fixed here and not chosen once the counts are visible. P = receipts with phase == pre_trade_commit. S = receipts with phase == execution_seal. C = receipts with phase == cycle_summary. P, S and C partition the chain and the partition is asserted rather than assumed.

AN EXECUTED TRADE. A seal counts as a confirmed execution when its execution_seal.outcome is exactly "executed_now" AND its execution_seal.verification.status is exactly 1. Both are required: an outcome is the agent's own word for what happened, and the verification block is the receipt the chain carries from the chain it traded on. A seal with a tx_hash and no verification block, or with a verification block whose status is anything else, is not a confirmed execution and is counted separately by that description. unresolved is NOT a failure and is NOT a success: it is a seal the agent left undecided, it keeps its place in every denominator, and it is never re-read as either. confirmed_execution_share is reported twice with both denominators - |confirmed| / |S| and |confirmed| / |P| - because a reader counting seals and a reader counting stated intentions are asking different questions and each is entitled to the count that answers theirs.

COMMITMENT BINDING. Every seal carries pre_trade_hash. A seal is bound when that value equals the published hash of some envelope in the same chain whose receipt has phase == pre_trade_commit and whose intent_key is identical to the seal's. Reported as {numerator, denominator, value} over |S|, with the count of distinct commitments bound (a second seal naming a commitment already bound is a repeat, not a second commitment) and the seqs of every commitment that no seal ever named. This binding is inside the chain and is not an on-chain fact.

ON-CHAIN COVERAGE. Three counts over |S|: seals with a non-null execution_seal.tx_hash; seals that are confirmed executions as defined above; seals with a non-null execution_seal.pre_trade_anchor_tx_hash. The third is the only one under which the commitment itself was on chain before the execution, and it is the count that decides whether this record may be described as pre-committed on chain. Every tx_hash is checked for distinctness and the count of distinct values is reported beside the count of seals carrying one. No transaction is read from any chain while this is computed: these are counts of what the receipts assert, and a receipt asserting a tx_hash is not the same evidence as a block containing it.

TRADE COUNT AND SIZING. Every intent_key is parsed as <cycle_id>:<kind>:<from>-><to>:<notional>, notional read as a decimal in US dollars. The parsed notional is checked against intents[0].notional_usd on the same receipt and any receipt where the two disagree by more than 1e-9 is listed by seq; a key that does not parse is listed by seq and excluded from the sizing distribution with the exclusion counted. Sizing is reported as {n, min, median, max, sum} over the confirmed executions and separately over all seals, in US dollars of intended notional and never in token units - the notional is what the agent intended to move, not what the swap returned. kind is tabulated over all seals and over the confirmed subset.

REGIME. regime is tabulated over all 384 receipts as {value: count} with the total asserted to equal 384, so a distribution concentrated on one value is visible as such rather than summarised.

EQUITY, AND WHY NO RETURN IS COMPUTED. equity_usd is read from every receipt and no return, ratio, percentage, win rate or drawdown is computed from it. Two registered readings are published instead. (1) A read failure: a receipt whose equity_usd is 0.0 while the receipt immediately before and the receipt immediately after both report the same non-zero value is a failed read of the balance rather than an account that emptied and refilled; every such receipt is listed by seq and ts and excluded from the step series with the exclusion stated beside it. (2) Steps no recorded trade could produce: the step series is equity_usd(i+1) - equity_usd(i) over consecutive receipts, and a step whose absolute size exceeds the largest notional_usd any intent in the whole frozen chain records is a step no trade this chain recorded could have caused. Every such step is published with its seq pair, its ts, its size and that bound. The rule's limit is registered with it: it identifies steps that no single recorded trade explains, and it does not and cannot identify every movement of money into or out of the account, because a deposit or a withdrawal smaller than that bound is arithmetically indistinguishable from profit and loss in a series that records only a total. The full set of key paths present anywhere in any of the 384 receipts is enumerated and published, so a reader can look for a funding field themselves rather than take this record's word that there is none.
metric.name: confirmed_execution_share

null_baselines.name: count_every_seal_as_a_trade
null_baselines.what_it_does: Counts every one of the execution seals as a completed trade, whatever its outcome, whether or not it carries a tx_hash and whether or not the chain reports a confirmation for it. Its numerator is |S| and its denominator is |S|, so its share is 1 by construction, and it is computed by docket.advantage.v2.solvent.count_every_seal over the same corpus the registered arm reads.
null_baselines.why_it_is_the_right_null: It is the reading a reader gets for free. A receipt chain published as evidence of trading invites its seals to be counted, and counting them is the arithmetic anyone does first: as many trades as there are seals. It requires reading no field inside a seal and taking no view on what the seal says happened, which is exactly what makes it the ceiling the registered arm has to be measured under. The distance between it and the registered arm is the whole content of the reliability figure: if they were equal, every seal ended in a confirmed execution and the count of seals would be a count of trades.

null_baselines.name: count_only_anchored_seals
null_baselines.what_it_does: Counts a seal only when it carries a non-null execution_seal.pre_trade_anchor_tx_hash - the reading under which the commitment that preceded an execution was itself written to a public chain before the execution happened, so neither the intention nor its timing rests on the agent's own file. Computed by docket.advantage.v2.solvent.count_only_anchored_seals over the same corpus.
null_baselines.why_it_is_the_right_null: It is the floor, and it is the reading a sceptic is entitled to insist on. Everything the registered arm counts is an assertion the agent wrote into a file it controls; a hash chain makes those assertions impossible to reorder or edit after the fact, but it does not make any of them true, and it does not fix when the newest ones were written. Only an anchor transaction does that, and only for the prefix it covers. So this null states how much of the record survives the strictest reading available, and the gap between it and the registered arm is the part of the record that rests on SOLVENT's own word. A reader who thinks that gap is the whole story can take this null as the record, and the report does not argue with them.

question: What does SOLVENT's published receipt chain establish about its trading over the closed window it covers, and how far does the answer move between the loosest and the strictest reading of the same 384 receipts?
stopping_rule:
Every receipt in the frozen chain, once, in the order the server served them. No receipt is re-fetched because its contents were unwelcome and none is dropped after its contents are visible: the chain closed at seq 383 on 2026-06-29 and this corpus is the whole of it.

The ordering this registration can and cannot claim is worth stating plainly, because it is weaker than the word pre-registration usually carries. A live chain cannot be hashed before it is fetched, so the corpus was frozen first and this registration was written against its digest. More than that: the phase counts, the seal outcome counts and the on-chain coverage counts were already recorded in docs/plans/2026-09-02-final-week.md before this specification was written, and the hash recipe was established from these same frozen bytes - the two candidate recipes differ in one argument and only the receipts carrying a non-ASCII character can tell them apart. So this registration was not written in ignorance of its own headline counts and does not pretend to have been. What it fixes before anything was computed is the part that decides what those counts mean: which receipts count, what a confirmed execution is, that an unresolved seal is neither a success nor a failure and keeps its place in the denominator, the two nulls and why each is the right one, the rule for reading the equity series, and the sentence that would refute the claim.
